title: The 5 Hottest Temperatures Humans Ever Made, Ranked (#3 Beats a Star)

scenes.text: The five hottest temperatures humans ever made, ranked. Number three already beats the inside of a star.

scenes.label: KSTAR · 100 million °C
scenes.text: Number five: KSTAR, South Korea's fusion reactor. 100 million degrees Celsius, held for 48 seconds in 2024.

scenes.label: EAST · 160 million °C
scenes.text: Number four: EAST, China's artificial sun. 160 million degrees for 20 seconds in 2021.

scenes.label: Z machine · 2 billion °C
scenes.text: Number three: the Z machine in New Mexico. Over 2 billion degrees in 2006, hotter than the interior of a star.

scenes.label: RHIC · 4 trillion °C
scenes.text: Number two: the RHIC collider in New York. 4 trillion degrees, about 250,000 times hotter than the centre of the Sun.

scenes.label: LHC · 5 trillion °C
scenes.text: Number one: the Large Hadron Collider. In 2012 it smashed lead ions together and reached about 5 trillion degrees. The hottest thing humans have ever made.

description:
The five hottest temperatures ever made by humans, ranked by peak temperature.
CERN's Large Hadron Collider reached about 5 trillion kelvin, perhaps 5.5 trillion, by colliding lead ions in August 2012; Brookhaven's RHIC made a 4 trillion degree quark-gluon plasma, roughly 250,000 times hotter than the Sun's core; Sandia's Z machine passed 2 billion degrees in 2006; China's EAST tokamak held 160 million degrees for 20 seconds in 2021; and Korea's KSTAR held 100 million degrees for 48 seconds in 2024.
Which number here surprised you the most?
first_comment: Guinness certified RHIC's 4 trillion degrees in 2012; the LHC's lead-ion run that same year came out hotter, listed as 5 trillion, perhaps 5.5. Which would you put at number one, and what should we rank next?
